description:
🌿 Team PAN — Ecology & Environmental Protection
We are developing the environmental section of the PAN & DAPHNIS educational app for students of natural sciences. Our AI mentor, Pan, helps users explore ecosystems, biodiversity, environmental protection, and field research. The app provides personalized learning resources, practical tasks, scientific information, and tools for environmental monitoring.
summary: We developed PAN — a digital educational platform and interactive mentor that helps students, pupils, and early-career researchers explore environmental changes using open NASA POWER data. The working prototype already includes learning modules, interactive climate indicator charts (air temperature, precipitation, solar radiation), a field journal, and a scenario-based assistant. The project solves the barrier of working with complex environmental data: scientific sources are often scattered, satellite and weather datasets require specialized technical skills, and academic theory rarely translates into hands-on research. PAN turns raw data into a guided step-by-step learning route—from selecting a specific area and building time series to testing the statistical significance of climate trends and formulating evidence-based environmental conclusions. This matters because addressing rapid climate change requires accessible scientific literacy. PAN democratizes Earth observation data, bridges classroom theory with field practice, builds analytical research skills, and fosters environmental awareness—turning Earth data into the ability to protect our planet.
details:
• What it does & how it works: PAN is a digital mentor and interactive educational web platform that turns open NASA climate data (air temperature, precipitation, solar radiation) into a step-by-step learning route. Users select a region, build time series, analyze trends guided by a scenario-based PAN Assistant, and log observations in a field journal.
  • Benefits: Consolidates scattered scientific sources into an intuitive interface, eliminates the need for specialized coding/GIS skills, bridges classroom theory with field practice, and features a live working prototype.
  • Expected Impact: Democratizes Earth observation data for pupils, students, and educators, builds analytical research skills, and fosters environmental awareness through local climate exploration.
  • Tools & Technologies: NASA POWER API for global climate datasets, statistical trend validation methods (Mann–Kendall test, linear trend with confidence intervals), and a web application hosted on Netlify (nasa-pan-2026.netlify.app).
  • Creativity: Blends a gamified "Environmental Trend Detective" journey and conversational mentoring with rigorous scientific methodology.
  • Factors Considered: The team addressed user barriers to reading raw satellite data, the importance of statistical significance to distinguish true climate trends from short-term fluctuations, local relevance (demonstrated via Cherkasy Oblast) with global scalability, and a phased MVP roadmap.
